speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history of a painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own, and now you are presenting with increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with episodes of pain during urination. To understand what is happening, have you noticed any redness, warmth, or fever accompanying these joint symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent history of a swollen left ankle that resolved, followed by right knee swelling and painful urination, along with your sexual history, I suspect this might be an infection affecting your joints. Have you noticed any penile discharge or urethral discharge?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (Reiter's syndrome) triggered by a sexually transmitted infection.
